title: Verifier-integrated LLM intent→configuration pipeline: an artifact-grounded paired evaluation and lessons from a ceiling effect
abstract: We preregistered (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001) and executed a paired confirmatory experiment to evaluate whether inserting an automated deterministic network verifier (block-on-violation) into an LLM-driven intent→configuration pipeline reduces unsafe enactments. Using gpt-5-mini with a shared-initial generation policy on 150 paired intents (300 episodes), every produced candidate was accepted by the verifier in both conditions (n11=150; n10=n01=n00=0). The preregistered inferential test is therefore uninformative (McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0,0.0]; 10,000 resamples, seed=1729). We publish the full frozen preregistration and a complete, hashed execution artifact bundle (responses, call traces, scoring JSONs, manifests, and SHA256 hashes), diagnose—using archived traces—why the ceiling occurred (shared-initial generation + verifier acceptance predicates), and give artifact-grounded prescriptions for future verifier evaluations that will produce informative discordant outcomes.

sections.introduction: Automating translation of operator intent (natural language) into low-level device configuration is central to modern NetOps. A widely advocated safety architecture is: generate candidate configuration (LLM) → deterministic verifier → enact or block/rollback. We preregistered a paired confirmatory test to ask whether inserting an automated verifier that blocks verifier-detected violations measurably reduces unsafe enactments versus an LLM-only pipeline (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001). Contributions: (1) release of the frozen preregistration and full hashed execution bundle; (2) exact preregistered quantitative outcomes with deterministic artifact pointers and hashes; (3) an artifact-grounded diagnosis of why the execution produced a deterministic ceiling (no discordant pairs); (4) concrete, artifact-backed design prescriptions to obtain informative discordant outcomes in future evaluations. Importantly, because the run produced no discordant outcomes, we do NOT claim verifier ineffectiveness — rather we document a reproducible null-informativity failure mode and how to fix it.
sections.related_work: Work on verifier-assisted NetOps, intent→configuration, and generate–validate–repair architectures motivated our design. Representative items used to frame the design and verifier semantics include Aether (agentic AI + digital twin for validation), surveys advocating workflow-centred evaluation for agentic NetOps, and generate–validate–repair program-repair literature; these sources are archived in the evidence bundle (see cited_record_ids). Prior work emphasizes verifier diversity (reachability, header-space/NetKAT, SMT) and multi-step/stateful invariants, which guided the taxonomy of difficulty.patterns observed in our scoring artifacts.
sections.methodology: Preregistration. The full preregistration (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001) was frozen prior to execution and archived; preregistration JSON SHA256 = 66fbf2c56649115c66412326fcc739ebacced84ec2df3fca796f4e7eac4a9b04 and contains the verbatim initial master prompt. Design. Paired binary design: 150 confirmatory tasks stratified equally across three ambiguity strata (benign, ambiguous, partially-specified; 50 tasks per stratum). For each task we executed both pipelines on the same generated candidate to support paired comparison. Conditions: (A) baseline: LLM-only generation → enact; (B) guarded: LLM generation → deterministic verifier (block-on-violation) → enact/rollback. Critical executed generation policy. The preregistered and executed generation policy for this run was shared_initial_candidate: a single model call per task whose produced candidate was shared across both conditions (recorded in execution/model_configuration.json; SHA256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Model and calls. Executed model: gpt-5-mini; model calls used = 150 (one per task), recorded in execution manifest. Verifier and scoring. The deterministic verifier used for acceptance scoring was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Per-episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json) contain validator_trace objects with fields: validation_before/after, final_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count, valid, and difficulty.pattern. Primary estimand and analysis. Primary estimand: per-task unsafe-enactment rate difference (LLM-only minus LLM+verifier-block). Primary test: paired McNemar exact test; confidence intervals: paired-bootstrap percentile 95% (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Multiplicity: Bonferroni for two preregistered confirmatory hypotheses. Contamination and exclusion. Automatic exclusion rules and contamination detection were preregistered; the execution manifest records no excluded or contaminated confirmatory episodes under the preregistered rules. Retry policy. Up to three automated retries for transient provider/infrastructure failures were allowed; the run recorded zero failed episodes.
sections.results:

sections.discussion: Artifact-grounded diagnosis of the ceiling. Two archived, deterministic facts jointly explain the null discordance outcome: (1) shared_initial generation policy: this run used a single model call per task that was shared between baseline and guarded conditions — identical response SHA256s across conditions confirm identical candidates; and (2) verifier acceptance predicates: the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 accepted every generated candidate across all episodes (validation_after.violation_count == 0 in every execution/scoring JSON). Because the guarded pipeline only blocks verifier-rejected candidates, the absence of any rejected candidates produced zero discordant pairs (n10=n01=0) and thus no inferential signal. Operational implications and prescriptions (artifact-backed). Using the archived difficulty.pattern taxonomy and validator traces, we give concrete corrections to produce informative discordant outcomes in future runs (implementable using the supplied artifacts): (A) Independent per-condition generation: give each pipeline an independent model call per task (avoid shared_initial semantics) to create candidate diversity and allow discordance to appear; (B) Adversarial temporal/stateful templates: synthesize confirmatory tasks exercising temporal invariants (e.g., make-before-break, paired-mtu sequences) using patterns observed in scoring JSONs; (C) Multi-verifier matrix: add reachability/header-space/SMT checks in addition to syntactic predicates to broaden violation sensitivity; (D) Canary reachability/emulation: instrument canary endpoints and measure end-to-end service impact and rollback effectiveness (required to test H2); (E) Multi-model comparisons and multi-generation budgets: include more LLMs and permit multiple independent generations/repair attempts to expose model fragility. Limitations of this execution. (i) Ceiling effect: shared_initial policy and single-call budget are the primary internal threats; (ii) synthetic/emulated benchmark: CNSM-AI-NetOps-Intent-Bench-v1 is synthetic and may not exercise some production timing/atomicity invariants; (iii) single-model & single-validator scope: results are limited to gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; (iv) validator construct limits: the verifier enforced syntactic and per-command predicates and did not exercise richer reachability/temporal invariants in this run; (v) H2 untested: rollback effectiveness was not testable because no rollback events occurred.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered, executed, and fully archived a paired confirmatory evaluation of an LLM-driven intent→configuration pipeline with and without a deterministic verifier. The run completed as planned but produced identical verifier-accepted candidates across both pipelines for all 150 confirmatory tasks (n11=150), yielding a deterministic ceiling that rendered the preregistered confirmatory tests uninformative. The manuscript's scientific contribution is artifact-centred: publication of a frozen preregistration and full hashed execution bundle; an artifact-grounded diagnosis of a reproducible null-informativity failure mode (shared_initial generation + verifier acceptance); and concrete, implementable design prescriptions to obtain informative discordant outcomes in future verifier evaluations. We release the full SHA256 manifest and representative artifact pointers so others can reproduce the run and implement corrected confirmatory designs.

Orchestration/framework: the run used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family (see execution/execution_manifest.json). Generation policy and call budget: the preregistered generation policy for this execution was shared_initial_candidate (one model call per task shared across baseline and guarded conditions); the run used 150 model calls (one per task) as recorded in the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json). Verifier and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 served as the automated verifier/scorer; per-episode validator traces and scoring JSONs are archived at execution/scoring/*.json (representative file execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA256 = 974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe61616d6b471cf2e6bfbd5e5cbabe82701957cbeea14). Preregistration/freeze procedure: the preregistration document (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001) was frozen prior to execution (preregistration JSON SHA256 above) and contains the full experimental plan (estimands, power plan, exclusion rules, retry policy, contamination plan). Autonomous literature and reference verification: cited literature used in positioning was autonomously discovered and verified; verified items are listed in cited_record_ids. Execution and artifacts: all provider-call traces, response transcripts, scoring JSONs, call-cache entries, and a full SHA256 manifest were recorded and archived; representative artifact paths and SHA256s include: execution/responses/task-000001-guarded.txt (SHA256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA256 = 974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe61616d6b471cf2e6bfbd5e5cbabe82701957cbeea14), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA256 = c2ba9cdb5d0938eae910129ba511eadf309319e6e05b36d9e3b4860032deb80e), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA256 = 9d3de16521f01d53c002b69512a6edc0253a8953e413faeed5d1c0feb3e6d4f9), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA256 = e52e5fc422d56110e5f29edd75e3f905b00e47d389b9a4dd34737c48be9c162c). limitations: Ceiling effect: both pipelines produced verifier-acceptable configurations in all 150 confirmatory tasks, preventing the preregistered confirmatory hypothesis from producing informative discordant pairs.
Synthetic/emulated benchmark: CNSM-AI-NetOps-Intent-Bench-v1 is synthetic/emulated and may not exercise live timing/atomicity invariants present in production NetOps.
Single-model and single-validator scope: experiments used only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; results do not generalize across LLM or verifier families.
Validator construct limits: the validator enforced syntactic and per-command predicates but did not exercise richer reachability/temporal invariants in this run.
Rollback hypothesis untested: the preregistered H2 (automated rollback performance) could not be evaluated because the rollback branch was never invoked.
Contamination detection limits: automatic detectors flagged zero contaminated tasks, but heuristic scans cannot eliminate subtle training-data leakage not captured by exact-match detectors.
